# SECURITY SECTORS The Commanding Officer divides the colony into four sectors. Changes are posted on the front page and may come at any change of shift. If a sign and a sentry disagree, the sentry is correct.
## SECTOR ONE [color=#9FC46A][bold]OPEN TO ALL CITIZENS[/bold][/color] - Living blocks, the canteen, the stores, the clinic waiting room and the bar. - No checks. Patrols pass through. Carry your documents regardless.
## SECTOR TWO [color=#F2C230][bold]CONTROLLED[/bold][/color] - Landing pads, fuel stores, the power plant, the air and water works, the radio relay and the colony administration. - Documents checked at the door. Bags may be searched. No loitering, no photographs.
## SECTOR THREE [color=#E8774A][bold]MILITARY[/bold][/color] - The garrison compound, armoury, vehicle park, command post and the perimeter fence. - Entry only under escort with a written pass. Sentries will use force to stop an intruder.
## SECTOR FOUR [color=#F4EFE6][bold]CLOSED BY ORDER[/bold][/color] - Declared in an emergency: a gas leak, a fire, a cave-in, a quarantine, unexploded charges or fighting. - Nobody crosses the cordon, citizen or soldier, unless assigned to the response. When the air is bad, the line is the line.
## MARKINGS - Chevron striping on a barrier marks the edge of a sector. - Hazard striping marks a checkpoint lane. Stop at the painted bar. - Flashing amber lights on a cordon mean Sector Four. Turn back.
Sector changes are also printed by the [netlink="Colony Herald" link="herald.colony.news"] when the press is on shift.
